# Editorial overview

| Problem | Tool | Output |
|---|---|---|
| A. GCD LCM Queries | Euclid and lcm formula | `gcd lcm` |
| B. General Inverse | extended Euclid | inverse or `-1` |
| C. Linear Diophantine | Bezout scaling | one solution or impossible |

# A. GCD LCM Queries

## Restatement

For each pair `a,b`, print their greatest common divisor and least common
multiple.

## Algorithm

```text
g = gcd(a,b)
l = a / g * b
```

## Correctness proof

Euclid's algorithm computes the greatest common divisor because replacing
`(a,b)` by `(b, a mod b)` preserves the set of common divisors. When the second
number becomes zero, the first is the greatest common divisor.

The formula `gcd(a,b) * lcm(a,b) = a*b` is standard from prime exponents: for
each prime, gcd takes the minimum exponent and lcm takes the maximum; their sum
equals the sum of exponents in `a*b`. Therefore `a/g*b` is the lcm. `\square`

## Complexity

```text
Time: O(q log min(a,b))
Memory: O(1)
```

## Full C++ solution

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int q;
    if (!(cin >> q)) return 0;
    while (q--) {
        long long a, b;
        cin >> a >> b;
        long long g = gcd(a, b);
        cout << g << ' ' << a / g * b << '\n';
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Full Python solution

```python
import math
import sys


def main() -> None:
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()))
    if not data:
        return
    q = data[0]
    idx = 1
    out = []
    for _ in range(q):
        a, b = data[idx], data[idx + 1]
        idx += 2
        g = math.gcd(a, b)
        out.append(f"{g} {a // g * b}")
    print("\n".join(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

# B. General Inverse

## Restatement

For each `a,m`, find the smallest non-negative `x` with `a*x == 1 (mod m)`, or
print `-1`.

## Algorithm

Run extended Euclid:

```text
a*x + m*y = gcd(a,m)
```

If the gcd is not `1`, no inverse exists. Otherwise, `a*x + m*y = 1`, so
`a*x == 1 (mod m)`. Normalize `x` into `[0,m-1]`.

When `m = 1`, the only residue is `0`, so the local problem prints `0`.

## Correctness proof

An inverse exists iff there is an integer `x` with `a*x - 1` divisible by `m`,
equivalently `a*x + m*y = 1` for some integer `y`. By Bezout's identity, the
set of all integer combinations `a*x + m*y` is exactly the multiples of
`gcd(a,m)`. Therefore `1` is representable iff `gcd(a,m)=1`. Extended Euclid
constructs such an `x` when it exists. `\square`

## Complexity

```text
Time: O(q log min(a,m))
Memory: O(1)
```

## Full C++ solution

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

long long egcd(long long a, long long b, long long &x, long long &y) {
    if (b == 0) {
        x = 1;
        y = 0;
        return a;
    }
    long long x1, y1;
    long long g = egcd(b, a % b, x1, y1);
    x = y1;
    y = x1 - (a / b) * y1;
    return g;
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int q;
    if (!(cin >> q)) return 0;
    while (q--) {
        long long a, m;
        cin >> a >> m;
        if (m == 1) {
            cout << 0 << '\n';
            continue;
        }
        long long x, y;
        long long g = egcd(a, m, x, y);
        if (g != 1) {
            cout << -1 << '\n';
        } else {
            x %= m;
            if (x < 0) x += m;
            cout << x << '\n';
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Full Python solution

```python
import sys


def egcd(a: int, b: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    if b == 0:
        return a, 1, 0
    g, x1, y1 = egcd(b, a % b)
    return g, y1, x1 - (a // b) * y1


def main() -> None:
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()))
    if not data:
        return
    q = data[0]
    idx = 1
    out = []
    for _ in range(q):
        a, m = data[idx], data[idx + 1]
        idx += 2
        if m == 1:
            out.append("0")
            continue
        g, x, _ = egcd(a, m)
        out.append(str(x % m) if g == 1 else "-1")
    print("\n".join(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

# C. Linear Diophantine

## Restatement

For each `a,b,c`, find any integer pair `x,y` satisfying `a*x + b*y = c`, or
report impossible.

## Algorithm

```text
g, x0, y0 = extended_gcd(a,b)
if c % g != 0:
    IMPOSSIBLE
else:
    scale = c / g
    x = x0 * scale
    y = y0 * scale
```

## Correctness proof

Extended Euclid gives `a*x0 + b*y0 = g`, where `g = gcd(a,b)`. If `c` is not a
multiple of `g`, no integer combination of `a` and `b` can equal `c`, because
every such combination is divisible by `g`.

If `c = g*scale`, multiplying the Bezout identity by `scale` gives:

```text
a*(x0*scale) + b*(y0*scale) = c
```

so the algorithm prints a valid solution. `\square`

## Complexity

```text
Time: O(q log min(a,b))
Memory: O(1)
```

## Full C++ solution

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

long long egcd(long long a, long long b, long long &x, long long &y) {
    if (b == 0) {
        x = 1;
        y = 0;
        return a;
    }
    long long x1, y1;
    long long g = egcd(b, a % b, x1, y1);
    x = y1;
    y = x1 - (a / b) * y1;
    return g;
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int q;
    if (!(cin >> q)) return 0;
    while (q--) {
        long long a, b, c;
        cin >> a >> b >> c;
        long long x, y;
        long long g = egcd(a, b, x, y);
        if (c % g != 0) {
            cout << "IMPOSSIBLE\n";
        } else {
            long long scale = c / g;
            cout << x * scale << ' ' << y * scale << '\n';
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Full Python solution

```python
import sys


def egcd(a: int, b: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    if b == 0:
        return a, 1, 0
    g, x1, y1 = egcd(b, a % b)
    return g, y1, x1 - (a // b) * y1


def main() -> None:
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()))
    if not data:
        return
    q = data[0]
    idx = 1
    out = []
    for _ in range(q):
        a, b, c = data[idx], data[idx + 1], data[idx + 2]
        idx += 3
        g, x, y = egcd(a, b)
        if c % g != 0:
            out.append("IMPOSSIBLE")
        else:
            scale = c // g
            out.append(f"{x * scale} {y * scale}")
    print("\n".join(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

# Testing discussion

The local checker compares against the reference construction, so fixed sample
outputs are one valid solution, not the only possible solution. On real judges
for Diophantine problems, either the output checker accepts any valid pair or
the problem asks for a specific normalized solution.

Important tests:

```text
coprime a,b with c=1
gcd(a,b) not dividing c
m=1 for modular inverse
large coprime values
```

# What to carry forward

GCD tells you what is divisible, extended Euclid tells you how to build the
linear combination, and modular inverse is just a special case of that linear
combination.
